translationRepairs: At first he was aide to General of the Soaring Dragon Dao Lin; with the headquarters he was transferred to aide of the Left Army of the Vanquisher of Barbarians, then External Gentleman Attendant-at-Court.

At first he was aide to General of the Soaring Dragon Daolian; with the headquarters he was transferred to aide of the Left Army of the Vanquisher of Barbarians, then External Gentleman Attendant-at-Court.
The source gives the personal name 道憐, Daolian; splitting it as Dao Lin is a romanization error.
He accompanied Dao Lin on the northern campaign to Guanggu and was enfeoffed as fifth-rank baron of Jiancheng County.
He accompanied Daolian on the northern campaign to Guanggu and was enfeoffed as fifth-rank baron of Jiancheng County.
道憐 is the same Daolian named in the preceding sentence, not two syllables belonging to separate words.
He was transferred to Central Army Aide on Dao Lin's Flying Cavalry staff and then Attending Gentleman.
He was transferred to Central Army Aide on Daolian's Flying Cavalry staff and then Attending Gentleman.
The staff is identified by Daolian's given name 道憐; Dao Lin is not a person in this passage.
In the third year of Yongchu he became Chief of Staff to Dao Lin as Grand Marshal.
In the third year of Yongchu he became Chief of Staff to Daolian as Grand Marshal.
The source again names Daolian as 道憐, matching the idiomatic translation and the surrounding biography.
After the vanguard under Dao Yanzhi and others was routed and pulled back, the next year he was again made chief of staff to the Grand Tutor, with his general's rank unchanged.
After the vanguard under Dao Yanzhi and others was routed and pulled back, the next year he was again made chief of staff to the Minister over the Masses, with his general's rank unchanged.
司徒 is the office Minister over the Masses; Grand Tutor would require 太傅.

In the sixth year (429) he was recalled due to age and illness, appointed chief of staff to the Grand Tutor under Prince of Pengcheng Liu Yikang, and given the additional title General Who Supports the State.

In the sixth year (429) he was recalled due to age and illness, appointed chief of staff to the Minister over the Masses under Prince of Pengcheng Liu Yikang, and given the additional title General Who Supports the State.
義康司徒司馬 means chief of staff in Liu Yikang's office as Minister over the Masses, not Grand Tutor.

The Founding Emperor appointed him acting aide on the Central Army staff, then aide on Dao Lin's Flying Cavalry staff; he inherited his father's fifth-rank marquisate of Jin'an County.
The Founding Emperor appointed him acting aide on the Central Army staff, then aide on Daolian's Flying Cavalry staff; he inherited his father's fifth-rank marquisate of Jin'an County.
The source names Daolian as 道憐; the idiomatic translation already preserves the name correctly.

Bandits in Guangzhou, taking advantage of the death of Inspector Xie Daoxin, rose as marauders and captured the prefectural city; Dao Lin promoted Daochan to General Who Quells Martial Disorders and sent him south to attack, but by the time he arrived Qianzhi of Shixing had already pacified Guangzhou, and Daochan turned back before reaching it.

Bandits in Guangzhou, taking advantage of the death of Inspector Xie Daoxin, rose as marauders and captured the prefectural city; Daolian promoted Daochan to General Who Quells Martial Disorders and sent him south to attack, but by the time he arrived Qianzhi of Shixing had already pacified Guangzhou, and Daochan turned back before reaching it.
道憐 is Daolian, the commander who promoted Daochan; Dao Lin is a mistaken split of his given name.
